executiveSummary: GM0553's 2025 identity, boundary, centre, 23,582 residents, 22 neighbourhoods and single BAG place are coherent, and the deterministic ten-preset, six-checkpoint, eight-service contract passes. Release is nevertheless correction-required. Lisse is a dense Bollenstreek municipality in Rijnland's managed polder/boezem system, inside dike trajectory 14 and dependent on Ringvaart, regional kades, polder pumps, sewers and groundwater. The canonical coastal preset reports 2.045403 depth-like inundation stress and 11,673 affected people-equivalent at T+24 without a selected North Sea defence failure, LIWO case or connected footprint. The river preset independently assigns 0.471305 m through T+72 without a Rhine/Meuse/IJssel or Ringvaart event; it must not stand in for local boezem water. Pluvial effects omit Lisse's official stress-test geography, eastern/southeastern water-on-street and groundwater mechanisms, and 25 assigned public water assets. Eight individual presets with nonzero affected values plus compound reuse essentially the same ten largest neighbourhoods. The road graph also overstates direct A44 access and omits the N207/Ringvaart/Lisserbrug structure named in municipal mobility evidence. At T0 the A44 main carriageway is open, but the Lisserweg underpass/local Lisserweg–Kaagweg connection remains closed until a dated reopening on 6 September within the final audit day; zero bounded NDW records do not mean open. Keukenhof's 2026 season is over at T0, but its 1.4 million seasonal visitors, 45% bus share and 2,000 seasonal workers demonstrate why scenario-date/event occupancy cannot be replaced by annual residents. Public assets, provider territories, one grid-planning point, antennas, schools and cross-boundary hospitals remain context, not live capacity or restoration. Exact hazard, service and T+72 claims require suppression or clear synthetic labelling; missing, empty, stale or out-of-horizon data remain Unknown/NoData, never zero, safe, open or available.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM0553 official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood, place, safety-region and statistics inputs
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; municipal/regional snapshots retrieved 31 August 2026; safety-region snapshot retrieved 2 September 2026
supports: Annual CC BY 4.0 CBS/PDOK inputs uniquely identify GM0553 as Lisse in Zuid-Holland and Veiligheidsregio Hollands-Midden, with 23,582 residents, density 1,502/km², 24.6% aged 65 or older and 3,886 one-person households. The reference point [4.543250983224523,52.256607020207944] is inside the 2025 generalized boundary.

Twenty-two neighbourhoods in four districts sum to 23,575 residents, seven below the municipal total (-0.030%); published households sum to 10,805 and rounded age-65-plus rows to 5,820. Deterministic allocation reconciles to 23,582 without rewriting observations.

One active BAG place, Lisse, is contained; BRT contributes Lisse and Halfweg woonkernen plus De Engel as gehucht. BAG/PDOK place data use Public Domain Mark 1.0. Place/settlement records are not hazard zones or event populations.

District-heating and public-charging fields are missing in 22/22 neighbourhoods and cars per household in two. Publisher null, suppression or non-applicability remains NoData, not zero. Annual residents omit commuters, labour migrants not captured at event time, tourists, pupils and care users.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Current water responsibilities, 2024 environmental vision and adopted climate-stress evidence
evidenceSources.edition: Current municipal water page and Omgevingsvisie Lisse 2024 inspected 3 September 2026; climate stress test adopted in 2021; blanket page/PDF reuse licence not stated
supports: The municipality defines its urban water system as sewers, public space and surface water handling wastewater, groundwater and stormwater. It maintains sewers, pumps, drainage and surface water and says very heavy rain can exceed sewer design; this is mechanism/context evidence, not live capacity.

The official vision links peak rainfall, high and low groundwater, drought, settlement and heat. It says Lisse has relatively high paving, especially around the centre, and that water nuisance and heat hotspots occur in multiple areas while clay/peat and bulb cultivation are drought-sensitive.

The adopted stress-test material identifies water-on-street and high-groundwater risks, including eastern/southeastern built areas and southern Poelpolder wet-season groundwater. The published map/model is planning/scenario evidence whose event, resolution, units, CRS, version, licence and NoData must be preserved before integration.
Policy ambitions to disconnect stormwater, add storage/drainage or combine works with reconstruction are not completed resilience, present pump operation or a T+72 recovery forecast.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — Ringvaart/boezem overload controls and Zemelpolder pumping context
evidenceSources.edition: Current authority pages inspected 3 September 2026; Zemelpolder maintenance page scheduled work November 2025–January 2026; blanket page reuse licence not stated
supports: Rijnland says the Ringvaart is part of its boezem and the current central system does not meet the legal water-nuisance norm for prolonged heavy rain. Water may rise enough to overtop a boezem kade or, in the worst case, contribute to failure. This does not assert a current failure.

Peak-storage deployment is not tied to one fixed level: the authority considers current level rise, forecast precipitation, prior soil saturation, wind setup and expected damage. The one-million-m³ Haarlemmermeer store and pre-pumping are conditional system controls, not guaranteed reserve for Lisse.

The current Zemelpolder page at https://www.rijnland.net/over-rijnland/wat-doet-rijnland/in-uw-buurt/poldergemalen/poldergemaal-zemelpolder/ says pumps maintain polder level and schedules replacement of the pump, inlet/outlet structures and access works. A scheduled January 2026 end is not live proof of completion, operation, capacity or backup.
The correct local causal chain distinguishes North Sea/primary defence, Ringvaart/boezem/regional kade, polder/groundwater, sewer/pluvial and water-quality/freshwater operations.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Time-scoped drought, freshwater, salinity and dike operational update
evidenceSources.edition: Operational update dated 2 September 2026; validity is the published situation, not evergreen state; blanket page reuse licence not stated
supports: On 2 September recent rain had improved conditions and enough freshwater was available to maintain levels, but low Rhine discharge still pressured supply. KWA-light remained active and could be adjusted as conditions changed.

Rijnland removed the Leidsevaart salt barrier on 2 September after water quality improved, directly changing a Bollenstreek operational state. Earlier closure, full KWA, pump shutdown, salinity and navigation measures are historic states and must expire.

Dike inspection was reduced to the most risk-prone locations; existing damage could still worsen and repairs/monitoring could continue into 2027. A regional statement is not a Lisse-kade inspection result or all-clear.

The update is source-backed operational context but not a Lisse rainfall, level, salinity, defence or inundation observation. It must remain affectsSimulation=false unless a governed adapter defines geometry, variable/unit, issue/valid time and event boundary.

evidenceSources.publisher: Veiligheidsregio Hollands Midden / Gemeente Lisse / WMCN-IPLO
evidenceSources.title: E05 — Lisse risk profile, public warning/72-hour guidance and LIWO interpretation limits
evidenceSources.edition: Current risk/guidance pages inspected 3 September 2026; LIWO release 2025.1.6 published 30 October 2025; local risk-page version/cadence and blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: VRHM places Lisse within dike trajectory 14 and characterizes flood probability as unlikely but impact as catastrophic. It also flags major events, labour-migrant housing, older/less-self-reliant residents, complex fire and strong road-disruption consequences. This qualitative profile is not a footprint or event probability input.

The current municipal ramp page at https://lisse.nl/diensten-en-informatie/zorg-ondersteuning/veiligheid/ramp/ identifies siren/NL-Alert, Hollands Midden Veilig/liveblog, broadcast, web/social and door-to-door/radiowagen channels. Listed channels are not confirmation of a warning, reach or completion.

The current Denk vooruit page at https://lisse.nl/diensten-en-informatie/zorg-ondersteuning/veiligheid/denk-vooruit/ recommends the first 72 hours and 3 litres of water per person per day. Guidance is not measured household stock, equal self-reliance or a restoration promise.

IPLO says LIWO is a WMCN professional flood-information system and requires specialist interpretation with water managers. A versioned expert-selected case is necessary before treating depth/arrival layers as a Lisse operational scenario.

evidenceSources.title: E06 — Current A44/Lisserweg works and Lisse access-corridor semantics
evidenceSources.edition: Rijkswaterstaat notice published 1 September 2026 16:08 local time; municipal mobility vision/planning material inspected 3 September; blanket page/PDF reuse licence not stated
supports: Rijkswaterstaat says the A44 main carriageway has been fully open since 4 July, while the Lisserweg underpass and Lisserweg–Kaagweg local connection remain closed until a planned reopening on Sunday 6 September. No exact opening clock is stated, so the transition intersects the final 72-hour day but remains planned until confirmed.

The same notice schedules Hoofdvaart underpasses/low bridge and Kaag direction ramps to close from 7 September, outside this audit's T+72 window. Future states must not be applied early and all states require asset, mode/direction, issue/valid time and confirmation.

The municipal mobility vision at https://lisse.nl/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2026/02/Mobiliteitsvisie_Lisse.pdf says Lisse's regional flows chiefly use N208 and N207, identifies the N207 Ringvaart crossing and N207/N208 junction as bottlenecks and describes weak A4/A44 connection. Keukenhof-season traffic compounds local congestion.

Monthly CC0 NWB generates two A44 and two N208 logical border links, all generalized scenario ceilings; it omits N207/Lisserbrug as an access dependency and can make a short A44 through-section look like direct municipal access. Zero bounded NDW records never means every road/underpass/bridge is open.

evidenceSources.title: E07 — 2026 season closure, visitor volume, bus share and seasonal staffing
evidenceSources.edition: Operator statement dated 11 May 2026; 2026 public season ended 10 May; 2027 opening scheduled 18 March–9 May; reuse licence not stated
supports: Keukenhof reports more than 1.4 million visits in the completed 2026 season, approximately 45% arriving by bus and staff increasing from 50 year-round to 2,000 seasonal workers. Aggregate season totals are not concurrent occupancy or a live count.

The 2026 public opening ended months before the 3 September T0 and the operator schedules 2027 opening for 18 March–9 May. Keukenhof visitor load must therefore be zero/not-active only for this dated public season state, not absent from all exercise dates.

VRHM separately flags annual large events including Bloemencorso. Event schedules, ticket/entrance counts, staffing, bus/coach staging and route plans need issue/valid times; annual CBS population cannot represent them.
No source establishes current emergency shelter role, evacuation capacity, crowd distribution, transport availability, medical posts, stocks or communications at Keukenhof.

evidenceSources.publisher: Het Waterschapshuis / Stichting Mijn Aansluiting / Netbeheer Nederland / RDI / DUO / RIVM
evidenceSources.title: E08 — Public water, provider, grid-planning, communications, education and acute-care context
evidenceSources.edition: HWH and public-context snapshots retrieved 31 August–3 September 2026; HWH CC BY-SA 4.0, Mijn Aansluiting Public Domain, DUO CC BY version unspecified, RIVM v1.1 CC0; exact NBNL/RDI reuse licence not established in consumed metadata
supports: HWH assigns 25 realized points to GM0553 using the 2025 non-generalized boundary: AWZI Lisse and 24 surface-water pumps. Fifteen capacity fields are null and ten non-null values lack unit/connectivity comparability. One adjacent Beekpolder point falls inside the generalized audit clip but is assigned to Teylingen, demonstrating why source boundary assignment must be retained.

A live point-territory query identifies Liander electricity/gas, Dunea drinking water and Ziggo telecom with provider update dates from September 2025 to May 2026; drainage is empty. One Liander planning sample, OS LISSE 10-1i, reports 44 MW existing withdrawal/injection and queues/projects, but is not live load, outage, spare capacity or municipality-wide topology.

RDI returns 29 antenna sites, DUO 13 education locations and the public-service register five locations. Points do not prove coverage/backhaul/power, shelter designation, occupancy, staffing, supplies or incident availability.

RIVM identifies no acute-care hospital inside GM0553. Straight-line centre distances are approximately 10.63 km to Spaarne Gasthuis Hoofddorp, 10.96 km to LUMC and 11.05 km to Alrijne Leiderdorp. Annual rooms/visits and roles are not route access, live acceptance, staff, backup or surge capacity.

Households total 10,805 and rounded age-65-plus residents 5,820; headline age 65+ is 24.6% and one-person households 3,886.

The planned Lisserweg reopening date falls in the last audit day but lacks an exact clock/confirmation. Only confirmed validity-aligned warnings, water controls, restrictions, care, utility, logistics and welfare actions may alter recovery.

corrections.summary: Add a role-aware Unknown-first T0–T+72 action/resource ledger for Lisse and cross-boundary dependencies.
corrections.validation: Every warning, water/defence/drainage decision, route/bridge/transit restriction, event/care action, temporary water/sanitation/power, repair, resupply and welfare action shows authority, trigger, issue/valid time, assigned resource, state and completion evidence; only confirmed valid actions alter recovery.

residualLimitations: No reviewed public source supplies complete safe-to-publish Liander/Dunea/gas/telecom/wastewater topology, live flow/load/quality/control state, backup endurance, priority users, crews, inventories or restoration estimates.

Lisse flood outcomes require distinct North Sea/primary-defence, Ringvaart/boezem/regional-kade, polder/groundwater, sewer/pluvial and freshwater/salinity scenarios with boundary, defences/controls, connected footprint, arrival and recession; generic depth is not a forecast.

The HWH register is contributor-dependent and fifteen of twenty-five assigned capacities are null; point status/number does not establish connectivity, comparable units, operation, reserve, power dependency or repair.

The Lisserweg underpass reopening has a date but no exact clock and remains planned until confirmed; A44 main carriageway, local underpass, Ringvaart crossings, N207/N208 and future works require separate scoped states.

Keukenhof season totals and VRHM event context do not establish concurrent occupancy, crowd distribution, coach/bus state, medical posts, shelter/reception, supplies or evacuation demand; the 2026 season is closed at audit T0.
CBS/BAG/BRT/DUO/RIVM omit live labour-migrant/visitor/commuter counts, assisted-evacuation needs, home care, hospital acceptance and household stocks.
Affected population is a people-equivalent scenario index and deprived person-hours is weighted local service deprivation, not casualties, evacuations, patients or customer interruptions.
Current water, salinity, dike, weather, route, care, event and utility state can change after completion; stale, empty, partial or out-of-coverage inputs must degrade to Unknown.
provinceReviewFlags: Define Zuid-Holland coastal-defence, Ringvaart/Rijnland-boezem, regional-kade/polder, groundwater and pluvial/sewer scenarios as separate source-specific mechanisms; do not reuse distance/population scalars.
Reconcile Lisse, Hillegom, Teylingen and Haarlemmermeer for Ringvaart levels, Kagerplassen/central boezem, peak storage, kades, polder pumps, Leidsevaart/salinity and first-72-hour controls.
Acquire the governed HLT climate-stress surfaces and retain native rainfall case, units, CRS/resolution, version, licence, sewer/groundwater inclusion, uncertainty and NoData.

Audit A44 through versus access semantics, N207/N208, Ringvaart/Lisserbrug and current Lisserweg/Hoofdvaart/Kaag works with asset-, mode-, direction- and time-specific operational overlays; repeated edges are non-additive.

Coordinate Keukenhof/Bloemencorso event-time occupancy, buses/coaches, emergency access, reception and welfare without persisting spring totals into September or conflating annual residents with visitors.

Coordinate Spaarne Gasthuis Hoofddorp, LUMC and Alrijne care access plus Liander/Dunea/Rijnland/telecom/supply continuity across municipal boundaries using authorized time-valid aggregates and Unknown-first actions.
